title: Weird Facts About the 30-Legged Bug in Your Bathroom ()
tiktok_title: House Centipede: The Leg It Drops and Where It Hides
tiktok_caption: house centipede in your bathroom 🐛 it can drop a leg to escape and usually regrows it by its next molt. Seeing lots of them may mean you have lots of other bugs. Stay or squish? 🐛✅ or 👟💥 #housecentipede #bugsinhouse #learnontiktok #thingslivinginyourhouse #meatballmyths

beats.say: Your bathroom bug can drop a fucking leg to escape you.
Each leg has a built-in breaking point.
By its next molt, it usually grows the leg back.
Those long things up front? Antennae that look like legs.
Predators struggle to tell which end is the head.
Its body is only an inch or so long.
Legs and antennae make it look three to four inches. Fuck no.
On females, back legs reach nearly twice the body length.
Babies hatch with just eight legs. Cute little bastards.
Growing up can take three years or more.
It hunts spiders, silverfish, cockroaches, even bed bugs. Badass.
It can catch several bugs at once.
It eats one while it holds the others. Holy shit.
But here's where the fuck it hides.
Dry floor drains. Under cardboard boxes. Crawl spaces.
It comes out at night to hunt.
Turn on the light, and it hauls ass.
Most house centipedes are never seen at all.
Some fall into your tub at night and get trapped. Dumbass.
Seeing lots? Shit. You may have a bigger bug problem.
They go where the food is.
Sticky traps show what it's been eating.
Dry the room. Fix leaks. Move the cardboard.
It won't harm your pets, clothes, or house.
It almost never bites. Mostly if you grab the fucking thing.
Usually it's like a bee sting. It can still swell.
So. Stay or squish? Don't lie.
